tier1.text: The extensor digitorum longus extends, or straightens, the second through fifth toes. This muscle also helps raise the front of the foot, a movement called dorsiflexion. The extensor digitorum longus sits at the front of the leg, between the knee and the ankle. This muscle runs from the tibia and fibula, the leg bones, to the second through fifth toes.

sentences.text: The extensor digitorum longus extends, or straightens, the second through fifth toes.

quotes.quote: A muscle originating at the lateral condyle of the tibia and the upper portion of the anterior margin of the fibula and inserted at the dorsal surface of the proximal, middle and distal phalanges of the second, third, fourth, and fifth toes which controls their extension.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov

quotes.quote: extension: movement in the sagittal plane that increases the angle of a joint (straightens the joint)
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The muscles in the anterior compartment of the leg: the tibialis anterior, a long and thick muscle on the lateral surface of the tibia, the extensor hallucis longus, deep under it, and the extensor digitorum longus, lateral to it, all contribute to raising the front of the foot when they contract.
